rows.title: A New Era of Bhaipo Politics — This Time From Suvendu’s House
rows.dek: The man who made the two words “tolabaj, bhaipo”, the slogan of a decade, now governs a state where his own nephew is the chief patron of a puja that killed nineteen people. Twenty-four hours later, the nephew problem remains unsolved. It has only changed houses — and the family firm he dislodged is already hurling his own word back at him.
rows.body: For the better part of ten years, Suvendu Adhikari had a one-line theory of everything wrong with Bengal. It fit on a flex banner, it rhymed at a rally, and it needed no footnote: tolabaj bhaipo hatao. Remove the extortionist nephew.
rows.author: Aaratrica Kashyap

rows.title: Ships Attacked Near UAE and Yemen as Iran War Widens
rows.dek: Maritime incidents near the UAE and Yemen have heightened concerns over shipping security as Iran’s parliament approves a new defence minister who warns the United States against further military action. Rising attacks around the Strait of Hormuz are adding pressure to an already disrupted regional energy and security environment.
rows.body: The latest incidents involve different vessels and different waterways, and the available information does not establish that they were carried out by the same actors.
rows.author: D. Chattopadhyay

rows.title: Joseph Kabila Joins Congo Rebellion, Raising Fears for Peace
rows.dek: Former Democratic Republic of the Congo President Joseph Kabila has emerged as the leader of a new political-military coalition challenging President Félix Tshisekedi. The Front for the Refoundation of the Nation replaces the AFC-M23 alliance, raising fresh questions about eastern Congo’s conflict and ongoing peace negotiations.
rows.body: The Democratic Republic of the Congo’s conflict has entered a new political phase after former president Joseph Kabila emerged as the leader of a new political-military coalition that includes forces associated with the M23 rebellion.
rows.author: D. Chattopadhyay

rows.title: Cost-of-Living Protests Sweep Europe as Public Anger Mounts
rows.dek: Hundreds of thousands demonstrated across France, Italy, Belgium and Portugal on October 17 over rising living costs, low wages, housing pressures and public services. France recorded the largest mobilisation, with clashes, fires and looting alongside demonstrations. The protests have increased pressure on governments to respond to mounting economic grievances.
rows.body: Hundreds of thousands of people took part in separate demonstrations across France, Italy, Belgium and Portugal on October 17, protesting against rising living costs, low wages, unaffordable housing and pressure on public services.
rows.author: D. Chattopadhyay

rows.title: SC Rejects Blanket Internet Bans for Children, Proposes Child Mode
rows.dek: The Supreme Court has held that children have a fundamental right to access and use the internet under Articles 21 and 19(1)(a) of the Constitution. Rejecting blanket bans as disproportionate, it favoured parental oversight, age-appropriate safeguards and dedicated child-mode settings while directing stronger action against child sexual exploitation material online.
rows.body: The Supreme Court has held that children, regardless of age, have a fundamental right to access and use the internet, warning that blanket restrictions imposed in the name of online safety are disproportionate and may expose minors to greater risks.
rows.author: D. Chattopadhyay

rows.title: 14 Dead, 28 Injured as Truck Mows Down Pilgrims in Gwalior
rows.dek: 14 people have died while 28 others suffered serious injuries after a paddy-laden truck ploughed into devotees near Sheetla Mata temple in Madhya Pradesh’s Gwalior around 1.30 am on Sunday. Police are investigating how the vehicle entered a restricted route during Navratri, while the driver remains at large.
rows.body: Fourteen people were killed and at least 28 injured when a paddy-laden truck ran into devotees near Sheetla Mata temple in Madhya Pradesh’s Gwalior district around 1.30 am on Sunday, October 18, as large crowds gathered for Navratri prayers.
rows.author: D. Chattopadhyay

rows.title: Chorbagan Stampede: Death Toll Rises to 19; Seven Arrested
rows.dek: The death toll in the Chorbagan Durga Puja pandal stampede in Kolkata has risen to 19, including four minors, while 25 others were injured in the incident on October 17. Police have arrested seven people, including two organisers, as investigators examine possible crowd-control failures and confusing announcements. A judicial inquiry and a wider safety review have also been announced.
rows.body: Nineteen people died and 25 were injured in a stampede at the Chorbagan Sarbojanin Durga Puja pandal in north Kolkata on Saturday evening, October 17, turning one of the city’s major festive gatherings into a mass-casualty incident.
rows.author: D. Chattopadhyay

rows.title: France Faces Major Unrest As Rioters Set Historic Limoges City Hall Ablaze
rows.dek: France’s cost-of-living protests escalated into violence on Saturday, with Limoges’ historic city hall set ablaze, shops looted and police injured. Authorities reported 1,200 arrests, while demonstrations also took place in Portugal, Italy, Belgium and Albania. The unrest has intensified scrutiny of public services, policing and France’s political climate ahead of the 2027 presidential election.
rows.author: D. Chattopadhyay

rows.title: SC Rejects Tamil Nadu Policy on Reservation After Conversion
rows.dek: The Supreme Court has upheld the striking down of a Tamil Nadu government order that allowed certain converts to Islam to seek Backward Class Muslim certificates based on their previous community status. The judgment examines how religious conversion, notified communities and constitutional rules shape eligibility for caste-based reservation.
rows.author: D. Chattopadhyay

rows.title: China Moves to Restrict Exports of 40 Technologies, Including AI
rows.dek: China has proposed restrictions or bans on 40 technologies spanning artificial intelligence, chip design, solar power and biomedicine, citing national security. The draft comes amid intensifying US-China technology competition, while a registration requirement for certain technology transfers has taken effect pending final rules.
rows.author: D. Chattopadhyay

rows.title: Nepal PM Shah to Visit India in Late November
rows.dek: Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah is likely to visit India in the last week of November, Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal has said, though no date is confirmed. Trade, transit, connectivity, energy and border issues are expected to feature in discussions, with both sides seeking practical outcomes and possible bilateral agreements.
rows.author: D. Chattopadhyay

rows.title: India Scores Zero in Six Categories of Global Climate-Health Scorecard
rows.dek: India is among the lowest-scoring countries in a 2026 global assessment of how national climate plans address public health. The Global Climate and Health Alliance identified gaps in India’s treatment of climate-related illness, air pollution, healthcare adaptation and worker protection, even as the country’s latest climate plan recognises health as a vulnerable sector.
rows.author: D. Chattopadhyay

rows.title: Jio’s ₹30,213 Crore IPO Sets Up India’s Biggest Market Debut
rows.dek: Jio Platforms has fixed its IPO price band at ₹1,065–₹1,119 per share, targeting up to ₹30,213 crore in what could become India’s largest public issue. The offer opens on October 21, with proceeds earmarked partly for repayment of borrowings at Reliance Jio Infocomm.
rows.author: D. Chattopadhyay

rows.title: Ankita Bhandari: Inside BJP’s Accountability Gap
rows.dek: An examination of 89 records involving BJP-linked political figures raises difficult questions about party discipline, legal accountability and the political careers that survive allegations of crimes against women.
rows.author: Aaratrica Kashyap

rows.title: FIFA Proposes $25 Million Payout for Each National Association
rows.dek: FIFA has proposed a $6.35 billion football development fund for 2027–2030, including an increase in planned funding for each national association from $10 million to $25 million. The proposal, linked to the commercial success of the 2026 World Cup, still requires approval and comes as president Gianni Infantino faces scrutiny.
rows.author: D. Chattopadhyay

rows.title: Shubman, Shafali Honoured With ICC ‘Player of the Month’
rows.dek: Shubman Gill has won a record fifth ICC Men’s Player of the Month award, while Shafali Verma has claimed her second women’s honour after a dominant September. India’s double victory follows Gill’s historic ODI double century and Verma’s all-round contributions to the Asia Cup and Asian Games triumphs.
rows.author: D. Chattopadhyay

rows.title: IMF Sees India Growing At 7% In FY27 And FY28
rows.dek: The IMF has raised India’s growth forecast to 7% for FY27 and FY28, citing resilient domestic demand and strong services activity. But the improved outlook comes with risks: retail inflation reached 5.54% in September, oil prices remain elevated, and the current account deficit is projected to widen.
rows.author: D. Chattopadhyay

rows.title: Worst Drought In 50 Years: 74% Of Maharashtra Affected
rows.dek: Maharashtra’s drought has hit 265 of 358 talukas, leaving fruit growers struggling to save grapevines, mango trees, pomegranates and banana plantations. With wells drying up and water becoming expensive, farmers face not only a lost harvest but years of potential losses if their trees die.
rows.author: D. Chattopadhyay

rows.title: 25 Years Later, How Much Has Modi Changed India?
rows.dek: Prime Minister Narendra Modi completes 25 years at the head of an elected government, from Gujarat in 2001 to New Delhi since 2014. India is now a much larger economy with wider digital payments, higher FDI, lower extreme poverty and stronger infrastructure. But jobs, wages, the rupee, inequality, manufacturing and institutional concerns complicate the record.
rows.author: D. Chattopadhyay
